text: The King's Land. The village of Oakstead — a half-day's walk from anywhere that matters.

speaker: Kai
text: Chanterelles by the fallen beech. Bilberries up the ridge, if the birds left any. Da wants willow bark…

speaker: Kai
text: …and Ma wants me home before the light goes. One of those is going to happen.
He knows this forest the way he knows his own kitchen. Everyone in Oakstead walks the woods. Kai is the only one who never learned where to stop.

speaker: Kai
text: Just to the ridge. …Just past the ridge.
The trees thin. A low shoulder of rock — and set into it, a cave mouth. Plain. Unremarkable. Every child in Oakstead has thrown a stone into it and run away. It has never once been interesting.

speaker: Kai
text: Huh. You've always been there, haven't you. And I've never once—
He does not hesitate long enough to talk himself out of it. He never has.

speaker: Kai
text: Five minutes. What's the worst a hole in a hill can do?
